desc: Derive closed-form theorem for the merge-orientation game — partially done: odd-N case proven (Aoki iff M odd); even-N case still open
Write brute-force memoized game solver for N ≤ 6–7 over all bipartite graphs to validate/refute candidate formulas
Run brute force and verify all anchor cases pass (especially N=4 M=0 ⇒ Takahashi) — anchors verified by hand-trace; odd-N hypothesis confirmed exhaustively for n=1,3,5

Derive the correct even-N merge game: model components as items with imbalance d_i = a_i − b_i; merging P,Q creates filler (cross−1) whose parity is (a₁b₂+a₂b₁−1) or (a₁a₂+b₁b₂−1) depending on orientation; the merging player chooses orientation, so the game is a parity fight. Need Sprague-Grundy or a pairing-strategy analysis on the multiset of components classified by (size parity, balanced/unbalanced).

Key subgame to solve: k singletons (1,0). Known results: k=1→no moves (T), k=2→Aoki, k=3→Takahashi (2 moves), k=4→Takahashi (4 moves forced by second player's pairing). Compute the pattern for k singletons via brute force for k≤7 and find the rule (likely periodic or depends on k mod some small number, with the second player able to mirror pairings).
Then generalize: arbitrary components reduce to the singleton game by treating internal filler S as parity offset and each component as a token of weight (a_i−b_i) mod 2 or similar.
Validate any new hypothesis against the full n=4 and n=6 brute-force tables before finalizing.
Add automated check comparing formula prediction vs brute-force winner for all enumerated bipartite graphs (n ≤ 5 or 6); iterate until exact match
Final implementation: DSU with bipartite coloring, compute (a_i, b_i, m_i) per component, evaluate validated formula in O(N α(N)), print Aoki/Takahashi
Edge-case tests: M=0 various N; single component; N=1; odd vs even N; already-complete-bipartite components (a·b = m)
